rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Foundry work can expose workers to molten-metal fume, spray mist and respirable crystalline silica from casting sand, fettlings and kiln linings.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: HSE identifies ferrous foundry fume as a lung-cancer hazard and pattern-assembly fume and spray mist as occupational-asthma hazards.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Inhaling respirable crystalline silica in foundry work can cause silicosis.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: HSE foundry guidance specifies task controls for pouring, casting, cooling, sand reclamation and other dust- or fume-generating operations.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Pouring, casting and cooling molten metal require effective respiratory-protection arrangements where exposure cannot otherwise be adequately controlled.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Sand-reclamation guidance requires dust extraction and supporting exposure-control measures.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Foundry controls should combine maintained engineering controls, supervision, worker compliance, records and health surveillance.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Health surveillance must be considered where foundry workers are regularly exposed to respirable crystalline silica and silicosis is reasonably likely.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: Foundry risk depends on alloy, process, sand and lining composition, temperature, ventilation, extraction, respiratory protection, maintenance and worker susceptibility.

rows.source: HSE foundry fume and silica control
rows.verified: HSE foundry evidence is process-, material-, workplace-, control-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: The decision to use a pesticide should follow a thorough risk assessment and form part of an integrated pest-management approach.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: The placing on the market, storage, use and disposal of pesticides are controlled, and only authorised products should be purchased for UK use.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: Pesticides should remain in their original labelled containers and must not be decanted into drinks bottles or similar containers.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: Pesticide stores should prevent unwanted releases, use suitable construction and be secured against unauthorised access.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: Pesticides should not be carried in a vehicle cab and should be separated from occupants in secure leak-resistant storage.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: HSE provides separate requirements for product labels, agricultural use, codes of practice, application equipment and spray-drift reduction.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: Professional users must follow product-label conditions covering crop or pest, maximum dose, operator protection, training and environmental protection.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: Workers should use supplied protective equipment correctly, avoid contaminated surfaces and wash protective clothing, gloves and hands after work.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: Pesticide risk depends on active substance, formulation, dose, application method, weather, storage, equipment, PPE, training and exposed people or ecosystems.

rows.source: HSE pesticide use, storage and disposal safety
rows.verified: HSE pesticide evidence is product-, task-, operator-, environment-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level poisoning probability.
